chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Jumhūr, from his father, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to punish a community that has adopted as its religion allegiance to an Imam who is not from Allah, even if it is righteous and Godwary in its deeds. And indeed, Allah is surely ashamed to punish a community that has adopted as its religion allegiance to an Imam from Allah, even if it is unjust and evil-doing in its deeds.

key_terms.أُمَّةً: a community or collective religious group
key_terms.إِمَامٍ: an Imam, meaning a leader whose authority is religiously binding
key_terms.دَانَتْ: adopted as religion; followed in a binding religious sense
key_terms.مِنَ اللَّهِ: from Allah; divinely appointed and authorized
key_terms.يُعَذِّبَ: to punish; to subject to divine punishment

ai.seo_question: Why does allegiance to a divinely appointed Imam matter more than outward righteous deeds?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the truth of divinely sanctioned leadership is foundational in religion, and that devotion to an Imam not appointed by Allah invalidates the religious standing of a community even if its outward deeds appear righteous. Conversely, adherence to an Imam from Allah carries decisive significance, highlighting the centrality of Imamate in Shia theology.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhour, from his father, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is not Embarrassed from Punishing a community which makes it a Religion with an imam (leader) who is not from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and even if they were righteous in their deeds; and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is too Embarrassed to Punish a community which makes it a Religion with an Imam<sup>asws</sup> from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and even if they were unjust, sinful, in their deeds’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Jumhur from his father from Safwan from ibn Maskan from ‘Abdallah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “Allah will not be ashamed to punish an ’Umma (nation) who has lived a religious lile under the guardianship of an unjust Imam who has said the following.would possess no authority form Allah even though such people would be virtuous and pious in their deeds.

However, Allah will be ashamed to punish a people who lived a religious life under the guardianship of an Imam who is just in his dealings and possesses authority from Allah even though they would be unjust in their dealings and have committed sins.”
